messages:
Incident Bot: ALERT: high KV cardinality + latency spike on ntk-prod (service: inference/rope-longctx). Paging oncall: @Maria Chen @Alex Wu @Samir Patel @June Ortega.

Maria Chen: Ack. Looking at graphs: total KV entries on primary cluster jumped rapidly 00:12 UTC, memory near 91%. 99th latency for rope-longctx routes climbed from 120ms -> 980ms.

Alex Wu: Joining. Correlating with recent model rollout (rope-longctx v2) and new NTK/YaRN sliding-window client behavior. Seeing enormous growth in unique KV keys under prefix sw:rope:ntk:ctx:hash*.

Samir Patel: Logs show many short-lived prefixes and extremely frequent writes to KV per partial prefix. Continuous batching kept partial contexts alive longer, increasing key churn. Hypothesis: combination of rope scaling + sliding-window key explosion + batching retention => cardinality storm.

June Ortega: Confirmed via redis INFO: keyspace notifications spiked, key eviction rate low because TTLs not set for sliding-window namespace. Also some clients are sending many small segments rather than consolidated prefixes.

Lena Park: CS check: three customers report degraded performance (acme-inc, pixly, tutorly). Notifying accounts with initial message.

CS Bot: Notified account owners for acme-inc, pixly, tutorly. Customers seeing higher-than-normal timeouts in inference calls.

Maria Chen: Mitigation options: 1) disable sliding-window feature for rope-longctx, 2) reduce continuous batching retention and max_batch_tokens, 3) apply emergency TTLs/eviction to sw:rope:* namespace, 4) temporarily route longctx traffic to smaller model variant. Prioritize least-impactful to customers.

Alex Wu: I'm going to flip the feature flag for sliding-window off for rope-longctx in the control plane. Command: curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/flags/rope_longctx_sliding_window -d '{"enabled":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer redacted'

Deploy Bot: Request accepted. Flag change queued.

Alex Wu: Flag toggle returned 202 and applied to control plane at 1769512420. Observing write-rate to sw namespace dropping ~45% within 90s.

Samir Patel: Next, reduce continuous batching retention: set continuous_batching.max_tokens=300 and continuous_batching.idle_retention_ms=80 on ntk-prod pools. Applying runtime config patch now.

Todd Rivera: Runtime patch deployed to ntk-prod-1..8 (rc change id: rc-1769512510). No service restart needed.

June Ortega: For eviction, I recommend a controlled sweep script rather than mass UNLINK. Running a batched delete script: python tools/evict_keys.py --pattern "sw:rope:*" --batch 500 --sleep 0.8s.

Alex Wu: Caution: large UNLINK storms previously caused redis CPU spikes. Use batch deletes and monitor CPU.

June Ortega: Running the script now (evict run id evict-1769512605). Deleting in chunks, monitoring redis CPU and latency.

Samir Patel: Observability update: 5xxs trend back to baseline, KV memory trending down from 91% -> 68% over 25 minutes. 99p latency falling toward normal.

CS Bot: acme-inc reports marked improvement, pixly confirms recovery. tutorly still investigating logs but fewer timeouts reported.

Maria Chen: Good. Keep sliding-window disabled and the batching caps for now. Plan further: implement prefix normalization to reduce unique key shapes, implement TTL for sw keys (default 5m), and add rollout gating that prevents unbounded key growth.

Alex Wu: I'll open an RFC for prefix normalization and change the sliding-window default TTL behavior. Also will add a synthetic KV cardinality test to our pre-rollout harness.

Samir Patel: Action items tracked: 1) Add default TTL to sw namespace (owner: June Ortega), 2) Add cardinality alarm (owner: Samir Patel), 3) Update runbook with safe-evict script and throttling guidance (owner: Maria Chen), 4) Add rollout rate-limiter to rope-longctx feature rollout (owner: Alex Wu).

June Ortega: Evict script completed: ~412k keys removed over 18 minutes. Redis CPU peaked at 62% during deletes. KV used memory now ~65%.

Lena Park: Updated customers with progress: acme-inc and pixly fully recovered; tutorly reports intermittent error rate but much improved. Account teams request a postmortem and assurance about future rollouts.

Maria Chen: Preparing incident summary and creating INC ticket. Severity judgement: Sev2 due to partial customer impact and degraded SLOs but no complete outage. Postmortem owner: Alex Wu.

Alex Wu: I'll take the postmortem. Rough RCA: the rope-longctx v2 rollout enabled sliding-window behavior that increased variability in prefix shapes for NTK/YaRN clients; combined with continuous batching retention policy this allowed a rapid ramp in distinct KV keys causing memory pressure and perf cliffs.

Samir Patel: Immediate mitigations executed: sliding-window toggle off, batching caps applied, controlled evictions, and alert suppression for noisy 5xxs. Follow-ups include TTLs, prefix normalization, synthetic tests, and rollout guardrails.

Maria Chen: Handoff to night oncall @Samir Patel. Please escalate to eng-sre if KV memory climbs above 85% again. I'll finalize the incident notes and link follow-up tasks.

Samir Patel: Handoff accepted. Monitoring dashboards pinned. Will notify if any regression.

Deploy Bot: Incident status update: mitigated. Flag rope_longctx_sliding_window=false, runtime config rc-1769512510 applied, evict run evict-1769512605 completed.

Maria Chen: Thanks everyone. Next steps: Alex to file postmortem by EOD tomorrow; June to implement default TTLs; Mike from QA to add synthetic cardinality test to staging. Update runbooks to include the batched-evict pattern and the batching cap quick-toggle. Closing thread after handoff confirmed.

Samir Patel: Confirmed handoff and will watch overnight. :thumbsup:
